What Sumizuri is, and what it is not
Sumizuri is an app, not a content service.
Sumizuri is a viewer. It shows the manga, comics, novels and videos you add yourself, and keeps your library, progress and settings.
It comes with no content, no sources and no repos. It shows nothing until you add something.
We do not host, upload, sell or hand out any content. We run no servers that hold content, and the app does not point you to any.
Sources and repos are made and shared by other people. We do not make, check, list or stand behind them, and we have no tie to the sites they reach.
A sync server is run by whoever hosts it. We do not run one for you.
Sumizuri does not limit what you add or open. What you add is your choice, and so is making sure you have the right to it where you live.
The sites a source reaches have their own terms. Those are between you and each site.
Sumizuri holds no content, so there is nothing in the app to take down. To have content removed, contact the site that hosts it.
The names of other apps, sites and works belong to their owners. Sumizuri is not tied to or backed by any of them.
Sumizuri is given as it is, with no promise that it works for any purpose. We are not responsible for what you do with it, or for what a source or a site does.
What stays on your device and what leaves it
Sumizuri has no account with us, no ads, no analytics and no tracking. We do not collect, see or sell anything about you.
Your library, history, progress, profiles, settings, downloads, logs and the cookies of the sites you visit stay on your device.
Backups are files you make. They go where you save them, and you can lock one with a password.
Sources you add ask the sites they reach straight from your device, as a browser would. Those sites see your IP address and can set cookies.
Repos you add are read to install and update their sources.
The app asks GitHub for new versions of Sumizuri. You can turn this off in App updates.
A word you look up in the reader goes to Wiktionary or Jisho. Web search opens Google.
On desktop, the first time a source needs it, the app downloads the browser it uses for sites with a bot check.

Sync happens only if you sign in, and only with the server you chose. Your library is locked on your device before it is sent, so the server cannot read it. The server keeps your username, and the name, type, app version and last seen time of your devices.
Removing a profile or the app deletes its data from your device. To delete your account on a sync server, ask the person who runs it.
